cells.tense: The looking here is done — you can lay a thing down with your hand open.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Put real figures on what you're paying for — hours in, or money, or days — and read what they say. Then set it down. The count finishes it.
cells.core:
When something here has been seen all the way through, you can put it down without a speech. It doesn't need to be small or finished — only clear. You take the last honest look, the hand comes away empty and uncurled, and that is the whole gesture. It reads as loss for about a day.

The pull is to hold on an extra beat — one more week, one more talk, just in case it means something different this time. It doesn't. The tally you run in your head already agrees with you; put it on paper instead. Give what you're spending a number, and let the figure settle it. What clears out frees up the hand that was gripping — that part comes back to you.
cells.sheetLine: You put a thing down once you've fully seen it.
cells.verb: seeing a thing through until nothing about it is left hidden
cells.place: at the point where the hand opens and something is set down

cells.tense: You are looking for the last thing there is to see, and there is always one more.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: This week, take any flicker that shows up and hold it a minute before you decide what it's for. Sit with it. Then do or don't.
cells.core:
Where this kind of seeing works, it often works too hard here. You take the final look and then take another, because a thing not yet fully seen can't be put down, and something in you is braced for the gap to stay open. So the hand hovers instead of opening. The examining goes on at the expense of the finishing, and the whole ritual turns into a way of not ending.

Nothing is gained by one more pass. The next new thing you notice about what you're holding — feel it before you name it or size it up. Let it arrive while it's still nothing in particular, and see what happens if you leave it undecided for an hour. Staying ready like that for a week costs you the certainty of one quick call, and it is the way out of the hovering.
cells.sheetLine: You look for one more thing to see so you don't have to end it.

cells.place: at the point where the hand opens and something is set down

cells.tense: You stopped looking at the thing long before, and the door it was behind is already behind you.
cells.act: hold the first resource in your hand before investing it
cells.ask: Pick a thing you've left sitting and hold it unnamed — no deciding, no using. Keep it in view for a day and feel that it's real.
cells.core:
The knack of seeing a thing all the way through and letting it go is yours, and here it has gone quiet. Nobody is holding the last look open — nothing is being examined and nothing is being set down. What you meant to decide about stays undecided, and the stuff it belonged to just sits. There is a blank page where the ending should be, and nothing gets its closing.

More looking won't bring it back. Pick a thing you've already left unattended — the loose end you keep rethinking — and carry it around, unchosen, for the day. Don't spend it yet, don't settle what it's for, just feel the weight and that it's real. Keep that up through the week without a plan attached. Form returns once the thing in your hand has been felt, and the setting down follows on a clock you don't set.

cells.tense: The endings around you keep completing while you say you are not the one who finished them.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Once today, stop and find something that was not here yesterday — a text, this light, your own tiredness. Name it to yourself and get on with the day.
cells.core:
Things around you reach their end cleanly — a job wound down, a tie finally named, a room emptied — and if a stranger wrote your history, these would read as luck. They aren't. The clear looking that finishes things is yours, and it is finishing things right now. You tell the story with yourself outside it, and the endings sit unclaimed when you were the one who looked hard enough to close them.

Meeting what arrives is how your part in it stops being invisible. There's no need to write the ending again; stand at the open door once and let the next thing enter on whatever schedule it keeps. Small as it is. Do that and the closed door stays closed, and you see your own hand on it.
cells.sheetLine: The endings are real and you don't count them as yours.
cells.verb: seeing a thing through until nothing about it is left hidden
cells.place: at the point where the hand opens and something is set down
